correctness.rationale: Let C be the n original core vertices of W(G), each with private leaf v′. A paired-dominating set must contain every core vertex: otherwise v′ must be selected to dominate itself but has no selected neighbor for a perfect matching. Conversely every set containing all core vertices dominates. Such a set is uniquely C∪L′, with U=C\L. Each selected leaf forces its core partner into the perfect matching, so W(G)[C∪L′] admits a perfect matching exactly when G[U] does. Its cardinality is 2n-|U|, proving the entire paired-domination set polynomial. The weighted matching polynomial z^n M_G(z) counts perfect matchings of G[U], not merely supports; coefficientwise inequality follows from p_G(U)>=1_{p_G(U)>0}. Equality iff each induced subgraph has <=1 perfect matching. Two perfect matchings differ by alternating even cycles; every even cycle (even if not induced) supplies two matchings on its exact vertex subset. For a forest, permutation expansion of det(zI-iA) permits only fixed points and edge transpositions and equals M_F(z). The spectral, root-location, and minimum-degree consequences follow. Independently enumerated every core graph of order n<=4 and all selected subsets of their whiskered graphs; derived full polynomials and support-vs-multiplicity inequalities from separately coded perfect-matching recursion. C4 gives strict z^4 coefficient 1 against matching coefficient 2.
residual_risks: The spectral identity is proved ONLY for forests, and no imaginary-root theorem follows for cores with even cycles.
The empty induced subgraph counts as having one perfect matching; necessary for all-selected-leaf top coefficient.

originality.rationale: Dettlaff–Raczek–Yero Lemma 3.2 already relates a CORONA minimum paired-domination number to a maximum matching; it does not give the complete paired-domination polynomial, exact even-cycle equality criterion, or forest adjacency-spectrum determinant. Xu's survey states the paired-domination definition and original 1998 reference without the claimed enumerator. The 2016 abstract titled Introduction to Paired Domination Polynomial of a Graph is directly related, but full text was inaccessible: the abstract alone cannot support an assertion that the complete paper does not cover this theorem; retain this as a material priority risk. Published complete-multipartite and chain-graph paired-domination polynomials concern different graph families; there is no inspected reduction that makes the fully whiskered arbitrary-G all-cardinality identity a corollary.
residual_risks: The inaccessible full 2016 paired-domination polynomial conference paper might have an equivalent all-cardinality corona result; its abstract cannot settle comparison. OA/arXiv full-text searches were unsuccessful and Oxford authorized access reported a disconnected VPN, so no full-text noncoverage is asserted.
Matching polynomials have several standard normalizations; M_G(z)=sum_j m_j z^(n-2j) is the positive-sign matching enumerator used here.
